reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from the same paper directly supports each premise: E1 reports fast segregation of Cr, Mn, Ni to grain boundaries causing ductility loss; E2 proposes and explains the precipitate absorption mechanism; E3 provides experimental confirmation that dual-phase samples avoid embrittlement at 600–700°C. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings without overstatement.
premises: Deformation at intermediate temperatures induces fast nanosegregation of principal elements (Ni, Cr, Mn) to grain boundaries in single-phase HEAs
This nanosegregation reduces grain-boundary cohesion and causes a ductile-to-brittle transition
Preexisting grain-boundary precipitates (e.g., Cr-rich σ phase) can absorb the segregating elements
Absorption by precipitates preserves grain-boundary cohesion and suppresses brittle intergranular fracture
The effect is demonstrated by comparing single-phase and precipitate-containing HEA samples tested at 500–700°C
